body_markdown:
Google AI Studio expanded Build mode in May 2026 to support native Android apps alongside its existing web app builder. The growing adoption of AI-assisted development is also changing how organizations approach software creation. According to McKinsey's 2026 State of AI report,[32% of respondents](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai) at organizations regularly using AI said their organizations had decided against purchasing at least one software product or feature because they could build it internally using agentic coding tools.


While the platform offers access to Google's Gemini models and Google Cloud integrations, builders seeking managed SQL databases, iOS publishing, or flexibility to use different AI assistants may want to explore alternatives.[Floot](https://floot.com/) is one option for creating and publishing full-stack applications.


This guide compares seven Google AI Studio alternatives for non-technical founders, small business owners, and entrepreneurs. Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot manages the infrastructure while the connected assistant handles development, within its available connector permissions.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build through your existing AI assistant** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) supports app development through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations without requiring a separate AI agent for standard connector operations.
- **Managed infrastructure simplifies full-stack development** : Floot provides[built-in infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting, reducing the need to configure multiple backend services.
- **Mobile publishing supports iOS and Android** : Floot offers[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) through native shells and supports TestFlight and Google Play testing workflows, subject to plan and developer-account requirements.
- **Pricing includes daily actions and hosting allowances** : Floot is free to start, with[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) that offer different daily build-action limits, AI credit allowances, and hosting allocations. Additional hosting usage draws from prepaid credit.
- **Code ownership remains with the builder** : Floot users own their code and data on every plan. Full project ZIP downloads are available on paid plans, as explained in the[export documentation](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) .


## **What to Look for in a Google AI Studio Alternative**


Choosing an alternative to Google AI Studio depends on specific full-stack development needs. Before comparing platforms, consider these core requirements:


- **AI model flexibility** : Can you use Claude, GPT models, or other AI assistants, or are you limited to a single provider?
- **Backend infrastructure** : Does the platform include managed databases, authentication, and file storage, or must you configure these separately?
- **Mobile app support** : Can you publish to both iOS and Android app stores, or only web and Android?
- **Deployment and hosting** : Is production hosting included with custom domain support, or do you need Cloud Run or external hosting?
- **Pricing predictability** : Are costs subscription-based with monthly allowances, or do they scale with token consumption and application usage?
- **Code ownership** : Can you export your full project and self-host if needed?


Google AI Studio uses Gemini models and can automatically configure Firestore (NoSQL), Firebase Authentication, and Cloud Run deployment for web apps. Its native Android projects use Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, with server-side integrations currently limited to its web app workflow. Organizations seeking managed SQL databases, iOS publishing, or multi-model AI flexibility may consider Floot, which offers a managed PostgreSQL database, mobile publishing workflows, and integration with[supported AI assistants](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) .


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that works with supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Users can[build and publish](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) applications through natural language conversations while Floot provides the managed infrastructure.


The connected AI assistant handles development through the available connector tools and permissions. Floot meters standard connector operations as build actions rather than charging separate AI model credits, while its optional AI agent and certain AI features consume Floot credits.


### **Key Capabilities for Full-Stack Development**


Floot provides managed infrastructure that reduces setup complexity for full-stack applications.


- **MCP connector for AI assistants** : Connect Floot to Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, or another compatible MCP client to create, edit, test, and publish applications through supported connector operations.
- **Managed PostgreSQL database** : SQL database with browser-based table views, query access, and database export on all plans.
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password login plus Google and Microsoft OAuth support without requiring separate OAuth app registration for those built-in providers.
- **File storage with CDN** : Managed storage for uploads and application assets with CDN-backed delivery.
- **Email and push notifications** : Built-in transactional email with message logs and support for web and native mobile push notifications.
- **Scheduled jobs** : Cron job execution for published apps on paid plans, supporting daily reports, data syncing, and cleanup operations without maintaining separate servers.
- **Payments integration** : Built-in Stripe workflows for checkout and subscriptions. Testing is available on Free, while accepting real payments requires a paid Floot plan and a connected Stripe account.


### **Mobile App Publishing**


Floot packages web projects as iOS and Android applications using native shells, supporting[mobile app publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) without requiring a Mac or Xcode. The Free plan includes 2 mobile builds per month, Pro includes 12, and Power offers unlimited builds.


Floot can upload connected builds to TestFlight and Google Play internal testing tracks. Connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan, while Apple connections are available on every plan.


App-store publishing requires separate developer accounts: an Apple Developer Program membership costing $99 per year or a Google Play developer account costing a one-time $25 fee. Floot handles build packaging and testing-track uploads, but developers must complete store listings and submit their apps for review. Final approval remains subject to Apple and Google's review processes.


### **Code Editor Integration**


Developers can connect Cursor to Floot through its MCP integration, continuing to code in their familiar environment while Floot manages the database, authentication, hosting, and deployment.


Floot also supports other compatible MCP clients, including VS Code and Zed. Available development operations depend on the capabilities and permissions exposed through the connected client.


### **Pricing Structure**


According to Floot's[live pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , the monthly plans are:


- **Free** : $0/month with 100 daily build actions, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, 2 mobile builds per month, and a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year.
- **Pro** : $25/month with 1,000 actions/day, a $10/month hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds/month, 5,000 AI credits/month, and custom domains.
- **Power** : $100/month with 5,000 actions/day, a $25/month hosting allowance, unlimited mobile builds, and 15,000 AI credits/month.


Annual billing provides two months free. Hosting is usage-metered, with charges above the included allowance drawing from prepaid hosting credit. Automatic credit reload is optional and disabled by default.


Model usage through supported AI assistants remains subject to the user's separate AI subscription or account limits. Floot build actions are a separate meter, and generating images through Floot or using its optional AI features can consume Floot credits.


### **Why Floot Fits Full-Stack Builders**


Floot is suited to non-technical founders, operators, and small business owners who want to create working applications with saved data, user accounts, and managed hosting without configuring backend services themselves.


Builders already using Claude or ChatGPT can continue working through supported connector configurations while Floot provides[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, email, payments, and deployment.


Its daily build-action allowances, mobile publishing workflows, and code ownership make it worth evaluating for business applications that need to operate beyond an initial prototype.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable (formerly GPT Engineer) is an AI full-stack builder for generating and publishing web applications.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable provides AI-powered web app generation with Supabase backend integration. The platform offers a direct connection to Supabase for PostgreSQL databases and authentication with row-level security.


Automatic code synchronization with GitHub repositories enables version control. Lovable supports prompt-based UI generation and iterative design changes. Managed hosting for deployed applications operates through Lovable Cloud with usage-based billing.


### **Key Features**


- **AI-powered web generation** : Describe applications in natural language and receive working web apps
- **Supabase integration** : PostgreSQL databases and authentication with row-level security
- **GitHub sync** : Automatic code synchronization with repositories
- **Lovable Cloud** : Managed hosting and backend services with usage-based billing


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable suits teams prioritizing web app development, visual iteration, and Supabase integration. The platform offers its own AI agent and credit-based development workflow. Teams evaluating existing AI subscriptions alongside managed infrastructure can also review the[Floot comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) to understand differences in building workflows and billing.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new, developed by StackBlitz, is an in-browser AI app builder for rapid prototyping.


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt.new generates working applications from prompts, with completion time varying by project complexity. The platform provides a complete code editing environment without requiring downloads or local setup.


Pro plans start with an allowance of 10 million tokens per month, with eligible unused tokens rolling over to the following month. Bolt Cloud offers built-in hosting with database, authentication, and deployment capabilities. Developers receive access to generated code for editing and customization.


### **Key Features**


- **Fast prototype generation** : Working applications from natural language prompts
- **In-browser code editor** : Complete editing environment without local setup
- **Token-based usage** : Monthly allowances with eligible rollover
- **Bolt Cloud** : Hosting with database and authentication
- **Full code access** : Export and customize generated code


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new fits teams that prioritize browser-based development and rapid iteration. Token consumption depends on the work performed, while Bolt Cloud provides managed backend capabilities. Teams comparing AI model billing and managed infrastructure can explore the[Floot vs Bolt](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) guide for a more detailed breakdown of the two workflows.


## **4. Replit Agent**


Replit Agent operates within Replit's established development environment, which supports a broad community of developers and teams.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit Agent provides a complete IDE environment with terminal access, package management, and testing capabilities. The platform supports languages and runtimes including Python, Node.js, Go, and Rust, beyond JavaScript and TypeScript.


The AI agent can perform multi-step development tasks with varying levels of autonomy. Managed PostgreSQL databases are included within the Replit environment, and deployment and hosting integrate into the platform.


### **Key Features**


- **Complete IDE** : Full workspace with terminal and package management
- **Multi-language support** : Python, Node.js, Go, Rust, and more
- **Autonomous agent** : AI handles complex development tasks independently
- **Built-in PostgreSQL** : Managed database within the environment
- **Integrated hosting** : Deployment capabilities included
- **Mobile development** : Expo-based workflows for supported mobile applications


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit Agent fits users who need multi-language support and prefer traditional IDE workflows. Its usage-based credit system means costs can vary with development activity. Teams considering whether they need a full coding workspace or a managed app-building platform can review[Floot vs Replit](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) .


## **5. Base44**


Base44 is a no-code app builder that was acquired by Wix in June 2025.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 generates web applications through natural language descriptions using AI-driven app creation. The platform provides no-code tools for non-technical users.


Built-in data storage supports application backends, while deployment and publishing capabilities allow users to share working web applications. Base44 also supports generating iOS and Android app-store submission files from published web applications on eligible paid plans.


### **Key Features**


- **AI-driven creation** : Natural language app generation
- **No-code interface** : Tools for non-technical users
- **Database integration** : Built-in data storage
- **Web deployment** : Publishing capabilities included
- **Mobile store files** : Generate iOS and Android app packages for store submission on eligible paid plans
- **Wix ownership** : Operates as a product owned by Wix


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 suits users seeking no-code web app development with optional iOS and Android store-file generation. Its mobile publishing workflow packages published web applications into native shells, with users responsible for submitting them through their developer accounts. For a closer examination of managed infrastructure and app-building workflows, see[Floot vs Base44](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual app builder founded in 2012, with a mature plugin ecosystem supporting web and mobile application development.


### **Primary Focus**


Bubble combines a visual editor and workflow logic with an AI agent that can build and edit web and native mobile apps from prompts. Users can work visually, with AI assistance, or both. The platform provides a drag-and-drop interface for building application interfaces.


A logic builder creates business processes and automations. An extensive library of community-built integrations and components is available through its plugin marketplace. Built-in database management includes visual data modeling. Tools support building responsive web applications and native iOS and Android apps.


### **Key Features**


- **Visual and AI development** : Drag-and-drop interface plus AI agent
- **Workflow automation** : Logic builder for business processes
- **Plugin marketplace** : Extensive community integrations
- **Database management** : Visual data modeling tools
- **Web and native mobile apps** : Responsive web and iOS/Android applications


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble suits teams that prefer visual development with AI assistance. The platform offers extensive customization through its plugin ecosystem but requires learning its specific visual interface. Workload-based pricing means costs scale with application usage.


## **7. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites is OpenAI's website and lightweight app builder that lets users create, preview, publish, and share interactive applications directly through ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites enables conversational app building where users generate and refine websites and lightweight web apps using natural language prompts. Built-in hosting allows eligible users to publish applications directly through ChatGPT without configuring a separate hosting provider.


Persistent storage saves application data and uploaded files between visits. User authentication supports visitor access controls and sign-in features, including Sign in with ChatGPT. Custom domains can be connected where the feature is available.


### **Key Features**


- **Conversational building** : Generate apps through natural language
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish directly through ChatGPT
- **Persistent storage** : Save data and files between visits
- **User authentication** : Access controls and sign-in features
- **Custom domains** : Connect owned domains where available


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites suits users who want to create and publish hosted websites and lightweight web applications within ChatGPT. Floot is another option for builders who want managed PostgreSQL infrastructure, payments, email, and iOS and Android app publishing while continuing to use a supported AI assistant.


## **Why Floot Works for Full-Stack App Development**


Floot is a[full-stack app-building platform](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) that combines AI-assisted development with managed infrastructure. Non-technical founders and business operators can describe applications through supported AI assistants while Floot handles the backend services needed to run them.


- **Existing AI workflows** : Build through Claude, Codex, Cursor, or compatible ChatGPT configurations using Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) .
- **Managed infrastructure** : Use built-in PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, hosting, and email without configuring separate providers.
- **Payments and subscriptions** : Add[Stripe payments](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) , including checkout and recurring billing, with a paid plan required for live transactions.
- **Cross-platform publishing** : Package web projects into iOS and Android apps, with supported testing-track uploads and separate store approval.
- **Search visibility** : Enable[SEO features](https://floot.com/en/seo) such as server-side pre-rendering, page metadata, sitemaps, and robots.txt.
- **Transparent billing** : Review[plan allowances](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for build actions, AI credits, mobile builds, and hosting, with additional usage subject to the applicable limits and billing rules.


Floot is free to start, and builders retain ownership of their code and data. Its connector complements existing AI development tools rather than replacing them. The available building operations depend on the connected assistant's permissions, while Floot supplies the infrastructure for publishing and running the application.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the main difference between Floot and Google AI Studio for app development?**


Google AI Studio uses Gemini models and can configure Firebase Authentication, Firestore, and Cloud Run deployment for web apps. It also generates native Android applications using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. Floot operates as a[full-stack platform](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) with an MCP connector for supported AI assistants, providing managed PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, and hosting. It also packages web projects into iOS and Android apps using native shells.


### **Can you use your existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription with these alternatives?**


Floot allows you to[build through AI](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) using supported Claude or ChatGPT configurations. Your connected assistant handles model usage, while Floot meters connector operations as daily build actions. Other alternatives have different billing arrangements. Some use separate AI credits or tokens, while ChatGPT Sites uses applicable ChatGPT and Codex usage allowances. Floot's plan fees, hosting charges, and optional AI credit consumption remain separate from your existing assistant subscription.


### **What backend services does Floot provide compared to Google AI Studio?**


Floot includes[managed backend services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including PostgreSQL databases, email/password authentication, Google and Microsoft OAuth, CDN-backed file storage, transactional email, and scheduled jobs. Google AI Studio can provision Firestore and Firebase Authentication for web applications. Floot users own their code and data on every plan. Database export is available on all plans, while downloading the complete project ZIP requires a paid plan.


### **How does Floot pricing compare with Google AI Studio?**


Google AI Studio provides free model usage quotas and an eligible Starter Tier that supports publishing up to two web applications without configuring a billing account. Additional API and hosting charges can apply depending on deployment and usage. According to Floot's[pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , Free includes 100 daily build actions, Pro costs $25/month with 1,000 daily actions and a $10/month hosting allowance, and Power costs $100/month with 5,000 daily actions and a $25/month hosting allowance. Standard connector operations do not consume Floot AI credits. Image generation and optional AI features can consume credits, while hosting beyond included allowances draws from prepaid hosting credit.


### **Can Floot turn a web application into an iOS or Android app?**


Yes. Floot packages web applications into native iOS and Android shells without requiring a Mac, Xcode, or React Native expertise. Its[mobile publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) workflow includes 2 builds per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Floot supports uploading builds to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks, although Google Play connections require a paid plan. Apple and Google developer accounts are still required, and users must complete store submissions and obtain approval independently. Google AI Studio generates native Android applications, while other alternatives offer their own mobile development or packaging workflows.
